title: Docker container OOM-killed
explanation: A Docker container was killed by the Linux OOM killer due to memory exhaustion. The container named in the match ran out of available RAM (or hit a memory limit) and the kernel force-killed it to protect system stability.

title: XFS corruption warning
explanation: Filesystem corruption was detected on an array disk or cache device. This is a high-severity finding — run a filesystem check on the affected device and consider replacing the disk if corruption recurs.

title: BTRFS error/checksum failure
explanation: BTRFS reported an error or checksum mismatch, often seen on cache pool drives. This can indicate a failing disk, a bad cable, or memory issues corrupting data before it's written.

title: Cache pool full
explanation: A mount point (often /mnt/cache) is out of space. Check cache drive usage and mover settings — if the mover isn't running or shares aren't configured to move data off cache, it will fill up.

title: Unclean shutdown detected
explanation: The system didn't shut down gracefully last time (power loss, crash, or hard reset). This forces a parity check on the next array start, which can take many hours on large arrays.

title: Network bonding link down
explanation: A bonded network interface lost link to its switch or peer. Check physical cabling, the switch port, and bonding/LACP configuration on both ends.

title: SMART reallocated/pending sectors rising
explanation: A non-zero reallocated or pending sector count was found in SMART data — an early warning sign of drive failure. Back up data on this disk and monitor it closely, or plan a replacement.
